text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- The army chief of staff wrote a series of letters earlier this month to then prime minister Necmettin Erbakan protesting at police personnel collecting information on the armed forces.
- State minister responsible for the economy Gunes Taner is preparing a six month shock programme to tackle the government deficit.
MILLIYET
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz has accused the security police under the previous government of setting up a special unit to gather information on the armed forces.
- Yilmaz's government is expected to announce an 18 to 20 percent salary rise for civil servants.
HURRIYET
- Yilmaz has vowed to clamp down on Islamist activism.
- The government has suspended all privatisation tenders until it receives a parliamentary vote of confidence.
YENI YUZYIL
- The husband of former prime minister Tansu Ciller has given testimony to prosectors over an alleged false testimony concerning the family's wealth.
- The government is to re-examine a number of state energy tenders awarded under the previous administration.
RADIKAL
- Police at the centre of allegations that they kept the army top brass under surveillance have said they were investigating the possibility of a military coup.
- Recent political controversy has made the economy resemble a ship without a captain.
ZAMAN
- Experts have said that police surveillance of the military as alleged by the secularist media is technically impossible.
DUNYA
- A report by the Economic Development Foundation concludes that EU member countries look positvely on Turkey's economy, but have doubts about its political stability.
